findings.title: upsampled_count ignores events with NULL sample_weight, so they are silently dropped
findings.body:
`upsampled_count` compiles to `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. ClickHouse `sum` skips NULL values, so any matched error without a `sample_weight` contributes 0 instead of 1. Such events include ones ingested before a project was allowlisted, ones sent without `error_sampling.client_sample_rate`, and rows from storages that never populate the column.

The comment says the schema guarantees `sample_weight`, but nothing enforces that; the allowlist is just a project-id option. Enabling a project would make historical buckets drop to near zero, and unsampled errors would vanish from charts.

Fix: aggregate `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` so unweighted events still count as one.

findings.title: Error-focused detection is a raw substring match and also matches negated `!event.type:error`
findings.body:
`_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query contains `event.type:error`. That is also true for `!event.type:error`, which explicitly excludes errors, and for `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` or a quoted message containing that text.

On the discover dataset those queries return transactions or mixed events. They would still be rewritten to `upsampled_count()`, summing a weight column that is absent or NULL for transactions, which gives wrong counts. The docstring claims this errs "on the side of caution", but the negated case is the opposite.

Fix: parse the query, e.g. with `event_search`, and require a positive `event.type:error` filter, with no negation and no OR containing other types.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset` and the raw request query instead of the dataset/query actually being executed
findings.body:
Inside `_get_event_stats` the eligibility check is passed the closed-over `dataset`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument. The helper also inspects `request.GET["query"]` rather than the `query` argument.

In the dashboard discover-split path, `_get_event_stats` is called with `discover` and a rewritten query (`({query}) AND !event.type:transaction`, or ERROR_EVENTS split widgets). The outer `dataset` there is always metrics_performance or metrics_enhanced_performance, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False. Error-only results for split widgets are therefore never upsampled, while the same query from a non-dashboard request is.

The same mismatch can let a transactions-only sub-query be judged by the original request's query text.

Fix: pass `scoped_dataset` and the effective `query` into the eligibility check.

findings.title: Stray submodule gitlink committed to the repository root
findings.body:
The PR adds `sentry-repo` as a gitlink (`Subproject commit a5d2909…`, the base commit of this repo) with no `.gitmodules` entry. This looks like an accidental nested checkout.

It creates a dangling submodule that breaks or warns in `git submodule` operations and CI checkouts that recurse submodules, and it has nothing to do with the feature.

It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: 60s eligibility cache is never invalidated and contradicts the 'fresh read' contract
findings.body:
The eligibility result is cached for 60 seconds per org and project set. `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere, and it cannot practically be: invalidation needs every project-id combination that was cached, but option changes are not tied to orgs or project sets.

After a project is removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, for example to roll back a bad rollout, its counts stay inflated for up to a minute. That inconsistency is per project set.

The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says the allowlist is read fresh each time "to ensure we always have the latest configuration state", which the caching wrapper defeats. The cache key also relies on the Python `hash()` of the project tuple, so distinct project sets can in principle share an entry.

Options:
- Drop the cache, since options are already cached in-process.
- Wire up invalidation and use the full sorted id list or a stable digest in the key.

findings.title: "Performance" cache adds a remote cache round-trip to every events-stats call
findings.body:
`options.get` is normally served from an in-process cache, so the check it guards is a cheap list-membership test. Wrapping it in `cache.get` and `cache.set` (memcached/redis) adds a network round-trip per `_get_event_stats` call, which is several calls per request in the dashboard-split and comparison paths.

The check also runs even when no `count()` column is requested. Net effect: added latency and cache load with no benefit.

findings.title: Top-events ranking uses raw count() while plotted series use upsampled counts
findings.body:
For top events only `timeseries_columns` are rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count`. `selected_columns` (from `field`), `orderby` (e.g. `-count()`) and equations still reference the raw `count()`.

The top-N groups are therefore chosen by raw event count, while the values shown are weighted sums. When events carry different client sample rates, the displayed series can be out of order or omit a group that would be in the top N by upsampled count. Equations based on `count()` will also disagree with the plotted count.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public user-callable function
findings.body:
Unlike neighbouring internal helpers, the new `SnQLFunction` is not marked `private=True`. Any user can request `upsampled_count()` directly in any discover-based query, including the transactions dataset where `sample_weight` does not exist. That produces Snuba errors.

The endpoint also bypasses all of the allowlist gating, so the function becomes part of the public query surface unintentionally.

findings.title: Public entry point, caching and negated queries are untested
